# Incident Report: Vidar Stealer Infection

**Evidence:** `2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (no IDS/Suricata export present in evidence directory — analysis based solely on packet capture via tshark)

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **192.168.1.216** | DHCP, Kerberos, HTTP |
| MAC address | **9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9** | Ethernet frames to/from 192.168.1.216 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** | DHCP Option 12 (hostname), confirmed by Kerberos `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$` machine account. (NBNS broadcasts show a visually similar name `DESKTOP-GXNYNO2` — a one-character NetBIOS rendering, same host, no other IP owns it.) |
| Logged-in domain user | **steve.smith** (domain **SPOONWATCH.NET**, DC `SPOONWATCH-DC` at 192.168.1.2) | Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString` |

The capture window is otherwise dominated by normal AD/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB traffic to the domain controller and Windows Update/telemetry traffic to Microsoft — i.e., a legitimate enterprise workstation with a malware infection layered on top. No initial-infection artifact (phishing email, malicious document, exploit) appears in this capture; the capture appears to begin after the initial compromise and only shows the post-compromise C2/exfiltration phase.

## 2. Malware Family: Vidar Stealer

**Attribution basis: behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No AV/YARA/hash-reputation lookup was performed (no internet access used per instructions), and no vendor label was observed anywhere in the traffic. The call is based on a distinctive, well-documented operational fingerprint:

- The infected host fetches exactly **7 sequentially-numbered files disguised with a `.jpg` extension** (`1.jpg`–`7.jpg`) from a single HTTP directory (`/osk/`).
- Every one of the 7 files is actually a **Windows PE32 DLL**, not an image. Internal PDB paths/import tables identify them as: `sqlite3.dll`, `freebl3.dll`, `mozglue.dll`, `msvcp140.dll`, `nss3.dll`, `softokn3.dll`, `vcruntime140.dll`.
- This exact 7-DLL bundle (Mozilla NSS/SQLite/VC-runtime libraries) is the standard set Vidar Stealer downloads on-demand to gain the ability to decrypt Firefox/Thunderbird-based NSS credential stores.
- Immediately after, the host **uploads** a single ~380 KB multipart POST to `/osk/` containing a ZIP file (`_5861695120.zip`) with the folder layout:
  `autofill/`, `cc/`, `cookies/`, `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`, `system.txt`

  This exact folder/file naming convention is the canonical Vidar Stealer exfiltration archive structure (browser autofill, saved credit cards, cookies, Outlook data, saved passwords, a desktop screenshot, and a system-recon text file).
- All requests reuse a fixed multipart boundary (`1BEF0A57BE110FD467A`) and a static, non-browser-typical header set (`Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`) across every request — consistent with a hardcoded stealer HTTP client rather than a real browser.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `2.56.57.108:80` (TCP/HTTP) — contacted directly by IP, no DNS lookup preceded it (hardcoded C2, no domain observed)

**Malicious URLs (gate `/osk/` on the C2):**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//2.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//3.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//4.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//5.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//6.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//7.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` (empty 200 response — bot check-in/config request)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (exfiltration upload endpoint)

**Malicious domains:** None. C2 was contacted by raw IP; no attacker-controlled domain appears anywhere in DNS traffic.

**Transferred files (downloaded modules, all served as `image/jpeg` but are actually PE DLLs):**

| Downloaded as | Size | Identified DLL | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.jpg | 645,592 | sqlite3.dll | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` |
| 2.jpg | 334,288 | freebl3.dll | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` |
| 3.jpg | 137,168 | mozglue.dll | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` |
| 4.jpg | 440,120 | msvcp140.dll | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` |
| 5.jpg | 1,246,160 | nss3.dll | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` |
| 6.jpg | 144,848 | softokn3.dll | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083` |
| 7.jpg | 83,784 | vcruntime140.dll | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` |

**Exfiltrated data (uploaded to `/osk/`):**
- Raw POST body SHA256: `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f` (379,629 bytes)
- Contains ZIP `_5861695120.zip`, holding stolen browser autofill data, cookies (Chrome and Edge, ~130 KB each), Outlook data, saved passwords, a desktop screenshot (`screenshot.jpg`, 271,977 bytes), and a system-info recon file (`system.txt`) — i.e., steve.smith's Chrome/Edge saved logins, cookies, and Outlook credentials were harvested and sent to the attacker.

## 4. Summary

Windows workstation **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), logged in as domain user **steve.smith** on the **SPOONWATCH.NET** AD domain, was compromised by **Vidar Stealer** (behavioral attribution). The malware pulled 7 legitimate NSS/SQLite/VC-runtime helper DLLs disguised as JPGs from `2.56.57.108/osk/` to enable Firefox/Thunderbird credential decryption, checked in via `main.php`, and exfiltrated a ZIP archive of stolen browser credentials, cookies, Outlook data, a screenshot, and system recon information back to the same C2 over plain HTTP on port 80. The initial infection vector is not present in this capture.
